pinyin: qióng zé biàn, biàn zé tōng, tōng zé jiǔ
literal: exhausted · then · change, change · then · get through, get through · then · last long
natural: When things reach a dead end they change; change opens the way; an open way lasts

meaning.en: When a situation reaches its limit it must change; change lets things flow again, and what flows can endure.
meaning.zh: 事物发展到尽头就必须变化，变化才能通达，通达才能长久。

equivalents: when the going gets tough, change course

examples.zh: 面对行业寒冬，公司引用“穷则变，变则通，通则久”，决定转型做线上业务。
examples.en: Facing an industry downturn, the firm quoted '穷则变，变则通，通则久' and decided to move online.

examples.zh: “穷则变，变则通，通则久”，改革的道理就在这里。
examples.en: '穷则变，变则通，通则久': that is the logic of reform.

story.en: The Commentary on the Book of Changes says: 'Where the Changes reach an extreme they change; changing, they get through; getting through, they last.' It gives the classic rationale for reform and adaptation.
story.zh: 《周易·系辞下》：“易，穷则变，变则通，通则久。”说明事物走到尽头就须变革，变革才有出路。

date.zh: 西周至战国 · 前9—前3世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Warring States, 9th–3rd c. BC

usage.en: Quoted in speeches, editorials and essays on reform and innovation; formal.
usage.zh: 常用于谈改革创新的讲话、社论和作文，书面语。

text: 博学之，审问之，慎思之，明辨之，笃行之
pinyin: bó xué zhī, shěn wèn zhī, shèn sī zhī, míng biàn zhī, dǔ xíng zhī
literal: widely · study · it, carefully · inquire · it, prudently · think · it, clearly · discern · it, earnestly · practise · it
natural: Study widely, question closely, think carefully, discern clearly, practise earnestly

meaning.en: The five steps of learning: study broadly, ask searching questions, reflect carefully, judge clearly, and put it into practice faithfully.
meaning.zh: 为学的五个步骤：广泛学习，详细询问，慎重思考，明确辨别，切实践行。

equivalents: the five steps to true learning

examples.zh: 校训刻着“博学之，审问之，慎思之，明辨之，笃行之”，提醒学生为学要循序渐进。
examples.en: The school motto reads '博学之，审问之，慎思之，明辨之，笃行之', reminding students that learning has stages.

examples.zh: 老师在开学第一课上讲解了“博学之，审问之，慎思之，明辨之，笃行之”的含义。
examples.en: On the first lesson of term the teacher explained the meaning of '博学之，审问之，慎思之，明辨之，笃行之'.

story.en: The Doctrine of the Mean says that the sincere person pursues goodness steadfastly: 'Study it broadly, inquire into it, think it over carefully, discern it clearly, and practise it earnestly.'
story.zh: 《礼记·中庸》：“博学之，审问之，慎思之，明辨之，笃行之。”

usage.en: Often quoted as a school motto or in essays on how to study; formal. Each of the five clauses can be quoted on its own.
usage.zh: 常作校训，或用于谈治学方法的文章，书面语。五句也可分别引用。

pinyin: xiū shēn qí jiā zhì guó píng tiān xià
literal: cultivate · self · regulate · family · govern · state · bring peace to · all under heaven
natural: cultivate yourself, order your family, govern the state, bring peace to the world

meaning.en: The Confucian ladder of duty: begin by improving oneself, then manage one's family, then govern the state, and finally bring peace to the world.
meaning.zh: 儒家由个人到天下的进阶之路：先修养自身，再管好家庭，进而治理国家，最后使天下太平。

equivalents: from self-improvement to serving the world
start with yourself, end with the world

examples.zh: 他从小就以“修身齐家治国平天下”为志向。
examples.en: From childhood he took '修身齐家治国平天下' as his ideal.

examples.zh: “修身齐家治国平天下”，一切要从自身做起。
examples.en: '修身齐家治国平天下': everything starts with oneself.

story.en: The Great Learning reasons in steps: only when the self is cultivated is the family in order; when the family is in order the state is well governed; when the state is well governed the world is at peace. The eight-character summary is a later condensation of that passage.
story.zh: 《礼记·大学》：“身修而后家齐，家齐而后国治，国治而后天下平。”“修身齐家治国平天下”是后人对此的概括。

usage.en: A condensed form of a passage in 《大学》. Used for the Confucian view of public service and personal ethics; formal, sometimes ironic when someone aims too high.
usage.zh: 由《大学》一段话概括而成，多用来谈儒家的修养与担当，书面语；有时也用于调侃志向过高。

pinyin: gǒu rì xīn, rì rì xīn, yòu rì xīn
literal: if · one day · renew, day · day · renew, again · day · renew
natural: If you can renew yourself one day, do so every day, and again every day

meaning.en: If you can make yourself new for one day, then do it day after day, and keep on renewing.
meaning.zh: 如果能有一天革新自己，就应天天革新，不断更新。

examples.zh: 清华大学的校园里有“苟日新，日日新，又日新”的石刻。
examples.en: The campus has a stone carving of '苟日新，日日新，又日新'.

examples.zh: 新年第一天，他在日记本上写下“苟日新，日日新，又日新”。
examples.en: On New Year's Day he wrote '苟日新，日日新，又日新' in his diary.

story.en: The Great Learning quotes the inscription on the bathtub of King Tang of Shang: 'If you can renew yourself one day, do so every day, and again every day.' It stood as a reminder to cleanse oneself of faults daily.
story.zh: 《礼记·大学》：“汤之盘铭曰：‘苟日新，日日新，又日新。’”相传商汤把这句话刻在浴盆上，提醒自己天天除旧布新。

usage.en: Popular as a motto of self-improvement and innovation; formal, often seen in essays and speeches.
usage.zh: 常作自勉和创新的格言，书面语，多见于作文和演讲。

pinyin: zhī zhǐ ér hòu yǒu dìng
literal: know · where to stop · and · then · have · steadiness
natural: once you know where to stop, you gain steadiness

meaning.en: Once you know your goal and where to stop, your mind settles and you can act with a steady purpose.
meaning.zh: 知道目标和止境所在，心志才会坚定不移。

equivalents: know your aim and your heart will settle
a clear goal brings a calm mind

examples.zh: “知止而后有定”，想清楚人生目标，心里就不慌了。
examples.en: '知止而后有定': once you are clear about your life goal, you stop panicking.

examples.zh: 他把“知止而后有定”写在书桌前，提醒自己别被琐事干扰。
examples.en: He put '知止而后有定' above his desk to keep himself from being distracted by trifles.

story.en: The Great Learning: 'Know where to stop and you will be steady; being steady you can be calm; being calm you can be at ease; at ease you can deliberate; and deliberating you can attain.'
story.zh: 《礼记·大学》：“知止而后有定，定而后能静，静而后能安，安而后能虑，虑而后能得。”

usage.en: Here 止 means the point of rest, the highest good one aims at, not 'stop' in general. Quoted in essays on focus and self-cultivation; formal.
usage.zh: 这里的“止”指应当达到并停留的至善境界，而非一般的“停止”。多用于谈专注与修养，书面语。

text: 秀才遇到兵——有理说不清
pinyin: xiù cái yù dào bīng —— yǒu lǐ shuō bù qīng
variants: 秀才遇见兵——有理说不清
literal: scholar · meet · soldier — have · reason · say · not · clear
natural: a scholar meets a soldier: right but unable to argue it out

meaning.en: Being in the right but unable to get a hearing from someone rough, unreasonable or with power.
meaning.zh: 理在自己一边，却遇上不讲理或有权势的人，怎么也辩解不清。

equivalents: you can't reason with a brute

examples.zh: 秀才遇到兵，他拿着合同去理论，对方就是不认账。
examples.en: A scholar meets a soldier: he went to argue with the contract in hand, but they simply refused to acknowledge it.

examples.zh: 跟这种蛮不讲理的人吵，真是秀才遇到兵。
examples.en: Arguing with such an unreasonable person is truly a case of the scholar and the soldier.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The scholar relies on argument, the soldier on force or plain stubbornness, so reasoning gets nowhere.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。秀才靠讲理，兵靠蛮力，所以道理讲不通。

pinyin: lǎo shǔ kěn shū běn —— yǎo wén jiáo zì
literal: mouse · gnaw · book — bite · words · chew · characters
natural: a mouse gnawing a book: chewing over every word

meaning.en: To be fussy about wording and pedantic about phrasing, often with a note of mockery.
meaning.zh: 过分斟酌字句，卖弄文辞，带讥讽意味。

examples.zh: 老鼠啃书本，他整天在咬文嚼字，却不管文章有没有内容。
examples.en: A mouse gnawing a book: he picks at every word all day and never mind whether the article has any substance.

examples.zh: 别跟我老鼠啃书本了，意思明白就行。
examples.en: Don't be so pernickety with me; it's fine as long as the meaning is clear.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The pun is on 咬 and 嚼, which both literally mean 'chew' (what a mouse does to a book) and figuratively 'pore over'. 咬文嚼字 can also be neutral, meaning to choose words with care.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。“咬”“嚼”既指老鼠啃咬，也指推敲字句。咬文嚼字有时也是中性，指措辞讲究。

text: 武大郎开店——比我高的不要
pinyin: wǔ dà láng kāi diàn —— bǐ wǒ gāo de bù yào
literal: Wu Dalang · open · shop — taller · than · me · 's · not · want
natural: Wu Dalang opens a shop: nobody taller than me

meaning.en: A boss who refuses to hire anyone abler than himself, out of jealousy and insecurity.
meaning.zh: 嫉贤妒能，不肯任用比自己强的人。

equivalents: a leader who won't hire better people

examples.zh: 他们公司武大郎开店，有能力的人都被挤走了。
examples.en: His firm is run like Wu Dalang's shop: every capable person has been pushed out.

examples.zh: 当领导的不能武大郎开店，要敢用比自己强的人。
examples.en: A manager mustn't be a Wu Dalang; he must dare to hire people better than himself.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Wu Dalang is the very short husband of Pan Jinlian in 《水浒传》; the story is that he would hire only staff shorter than himself. Used of petty, jealous managers.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。武大郎是《水浒传》中身材矮小的人物，传说他开店只雇比他矮的伙计。多讽刺心胸狭窄的管理者。

pinyin: zhōu yú dǎ huáng gài —— yuàn dǎ yuàn ái
literal: Zhou Yu · beat · Huang Gai — willing · beat · willing · take
natural: Zhou Yu beats Huang Gai: one willing to hit, one willing to be hit

meaning.en: A situation where both sides agree to it, so no one else has any business objecting.
meaning.zh: 双方心甘情愿，旁人无权干涉。

equivalents: both sides are willing, so no complaints

examples.zh: 周瑜打黄盖，两个人你情我愿，别人管不着。
examples.en: It's a case of Zhou Yu beating Huang Gai: both are willing, so it's nobody else's business.

examples.zh: 她愿意帮他，他也愿意接受，真是周瑜打黄盖。
examples.en: She's glad to help and he's glad to accept: willing hitter, willing victim.

story.en: To prepare the fire attack at Red Cliff, Zhou Yu publicly had the veteran general Huang Gai flogged for opposing him, so that Huang's offer to defect to Cao Cao would look genuine; Huang took the beating willingly.
story.zh: 赤壁之战前，周瑜故意当众杖责黄盖，使黄盖向曹操诈降显得可信，黄盖甘愿受刑。

date.en: late Yuan to early Ming, 14th c.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. In 《三国演义》 chapter 46 the general Huang Gai agrees to be flogged in front of the army so that his false surrender will convince Cao Cao. Usually said with a touch of humour.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。《三国演义》第四十六回，黄盖为让曹操相信自己诈降，甘愿受周瑜杖责。多带诙谐意味。
